Like `source:` the array is resolved lazily and never inlined. An in-study ``experiment`` reference also registers the workflow dependency. Mutually exclusive with `value:`/`source:`/`producer:`.
Bind the key to a computed scalar in a result container (same reference form a figure Layer uses, and the same PROV edge). Mutually exclusive with ``value`` and ``count``.

A labelled array sourced from another experiment's result, a dataset, or a curated entity — the cross-container form of a value (WHERE + WHICH + SLICE, PROV ``prov:used``). Mutually exclusive with ``value``; an in-study ``experiment`` reference also registers the workflow dependency so the source runs first. Resolved lazily, never inlined into generated code.

WHERE + WHICH + SLICE for a template edge whose whole matrix is read rather than stored or computed: another network's layer, an analysis result, or a cohort member's own connectome (``used: {cohort: <id>, query: {...}, output: weight, reconcile: by_label}``). Inside a per-subject run a cohort reference resolves to that run's subject, which is what binds a model network to each subject's own connectivity. ``reconcile: by_label`` aligns the read matrix to this network's node order through its atlas aliases. Resolved lazily and never inlined, and it wins over a same-named layer in the companion file. Mutually exclusive with ``producer:``.
The p-value, a scalar in a result container (same reference form a Layer uses, and the same PROV edge).
IRIs of the inputs, outputs and environment the activity consumed (BEP028 ``Used``).

Bind the annotation to a scalar in a result container (same reference form a Layer uses, and the same PROV edge). The referenced value is formatted through `text` at render time, so a statistic printed on a panel is computed, never transcribed.
The label. With `used:` it is a Python format string applied to the referenced value, e.g. 'r = {:.2f}'.
Horizontal alignment against (x, y) — left, center, right. Defaults to center.

Asterisks set after the text for a p-value READ from a result, as a paper prints `r=0.89***`. On the panel only: a caption states a test in words, so a `placement: caption` annotation that declares one is refused.

Draw an arrow POINTING AT (x, y), starting (dx, dy) away from it in axes fractions — e.g. [-0.08, 0.06] for one coming from the upper left. The text, when non-empty, sits at the tail. This is how a paper's callout arrowheads are declared instead of drawn in code.

comment.en: Parameter (CURIE into the per-model parameter namespace) along which the bifurcation is observed.

definition.value: Which part of a generated report this belongs in — the main Methods or the supplementary material. Placement only: every experiment runs and every figure renders regardless, so demoting one never changes what is computed. It answers a different question from a replication's target tier (how central a claim is) and from the source paper's own Fig/EDF numbering (where *they* printed it), because our document may carry a headline result's parameter dump in the SI, or relegate a figure the paper printed up front. Defaults to ``main``, so a recipe that says nothing keeps everything in the Methods.
Honest-placeholder text drawn when this panel's data is missing or degenerate (never a source-replot). Setting it wraps the draw so a missing container falls back to this label instead of erroring.

HOW to compute this value, when it is derived rather than obtained — the callable that produces it, its arguments, and (via `output:`) which entry to take from a callable returning several named arrays. The callable resolves against the recipe's `code_source`. Use instead of `source:` for a value that is a deterministic function of the spec's own inputs (a mesh operator, a template matrix): declaring the producer keeps the spec the single source of truth, where pointing at a pre-built file would let the two drift apart silently — and would need a prep step run by hand before the spec could execute. The result is cached and invalidated by the artifact fingerprint, so it is computed once rather than per run. On a `Parameter` it produces the value; on an `Edge` it produces the whole template matrix, which is what lets a connectome or a discrete differential operator be declared rather than pre-built. Mutually exclusive with `value:`/`source:`.
Bifurcation detection level. 0 = off, 1 = eigenvalues only, 2 = detect, 3 = locate precisely.
Number of eigenvalues to compute. Must be >= number of state variables for reliable Hopf detection.
Initial arc-length step size.
Enable fold (limit point) detection.

The parameters the continuation holds to a target while it varies its free parameter, as feedback inhibition control holds J_i: each names the parameter and the algorithm whose objective states the target. The continued system gains each held parameter as an unknown whose equation is that objective's residual. Refused when the objective states no target_variable and target_value, when no update rule of the algorithm targets the parameter, and on a continuation backend that holds no parameters (bifurcationkit holds them).
Tolerance on real part of eigenvalue for stability boundary.
Add the location of the data file containing the parcellation terminology.

How to turn an `image` panel's HTML/URL `source` into its `path`: the headless-browser recipe (viewport, scale, wait, clip). The declarative form of code/capture-screenshots.py, so a screenshot regenerates from the spec instead of being hand-captured. Ignored when `source` is a static file or a script.
Child branches to continue from detected bifurcation points (PO from Hopf, fold continuation, etc.).
Number of eigenvalue sign inversions to flag a bifurcation. Must be even. Higher = fewer false positives.

Absolute tolerance on the residual at which the Newton corrector has converged: the norm of the right-hand side f(x, p) at the corrected point must fall below it, in the units of f. BifurcationKit.jl applies it as that bound (NewtonPar tol). AUTO-07p tests the size of each Newton correction instead, relative to the size of the solution, so the AUTO-07p backends (auto-07p and pyrates-bifurcation) set both of its relative criteria to it, EPSL on the parameter and EPSU on the state, and only approximate the residual bound: a correction and the residual it removes differ by the conditioning of the Jacobian. Unset, each backend keeps its own default, BifurcationKit.jl 1e-12 on the residual and AUTO-07p 1e-7 on the correction. A branch's nested continuation that leaves it unset takes its parent's.

Maximum Newton corrector iterations per step: NewtonPar max_iterations on BifurcationKit.jl, and both ITNW and ITMX on the AUTO-07p backends. Unset, each backend keeps its own default, BifurcationKit.jl 25 and AUTO-07p ITNW 5 and ITMX 9. A branch's nested continuation that leaves it unset takes its parent's.

A `grid`'s cells stated one at a time, for a grid whose cells differ — a first cell showing the bare mesh the rest are maps on, or a row pairing two kinds. Each is merged over `cell:`, and carries its own layers. Mutually exclusive with `layers:`, which is the compact form of the same thing.

Numeric, string, or boolean value, OR an array (nested list) for array-valued constants such as mode-coupling coefficient matrices. ScalarValue accepts any literal primitive type, allowing parameters to carry control flags (e.g., booleans) or symbolic placeholders alongside numeric defaults.
Maximum continuation steps.
Globally unique identifier for the entity.
Dynamics model governing this node's behavior. Can be a reference (by name) or inline definition. If not provided, uses experiment's dynamics.
Maximum adaptive step size.
Minimum adaptive step size.
Maximum bisection steps for bifurcation point localization.

What every cell of a `grid` is: the kind they all draw, and the opts they share. Each entry in `layers:` then fills one cell with this template, which is why a grid of twenty surfaces needs the surface declared once. Its `bounds` stay unset — the grid positions its cells.

Sub-axes drawn inside this panel after its own body — the zoom windows, corner thumbnails and small key maps papers place over a plot. Declaring them keeps a panel that needs one from becoming a custom callable, which would take its whole interior out of the grammar.
Subjects in a dataset.

The panel letter to draw, overriding the mosaic key, or the string 'false' to draw none. Needed whenever the paper's panels do not map one-to-one onto mosaic cells: a row of five mode surfaces under a single (a), or a schematic cell that carries no letter of its own. Without it a grouped figure numbers every cell and its letters stop matching the paper's.

Whether to include this element in simulation output files. Applicable to state variables (default true), derived variables (default false), and network nodes (default true). On an observation it forces (true) or suppresses (false) persistence in the result; left unset, a terminal observation (one not consumed by another observation or a loss) is recorded and an intermediate one is not. Set false to suppress recording.

Names of observations to compute and record at EACH grid point, stacked over the sweep into one array per name. Entries may be derived observations (e.g. `loss`) or `analysis` diagnostics (e.g. `ad_gradient`, `fd_gradient`, `lyapunov`) — this is how a sweep of the diagnostics themselves is declared, replacing any per-point Python driver. Complementary to `observable` (a single scalar reduction); when both are absent the full observation Bunch is recorded.

Optional finer-scale Network that "lives inside" this Node (network-of-networks / multi-scale primitive). The subnetwork's nodes map (one-to-many) to this single parent Node. Cross-scale signal flow is declared as ordinary Edges in the subnetwork's `edges` list, using `source_network` / `target_network` with the `parent` sentinel to traverse up the hierarchy. The subnetwork may carry its own `graph_generator` (discrete sub-network — reservoir, spiking population, jaxley compartments) and/or `mesh` (continuous surface field) — one unified slot for reservoirs-per-region, spiking-populations-per-region, cells-per-region, and surface-mesh-patches-per-region. Recursive: a subnetwork's Nodes can themselves carry subnetworks.
Globally unique identifier for the entity.
Software requirements for the workflow environment; overrides ``experiment.environment.requirements`` when set.
Execution environment (collection of requirements).

What every cell of a `grid` is: the kind they all draw, and the opts they share. Each entry in `layers:` then fills one cell with this template, which is why a grid of twenty surfaces needs the surface declared once. Its `bounds` stay unset — the grid positions its cells.

Conditional logic for piecewise equations — the one place a piecewise definition is written, for a state variable, a derived variable or a derived parameter alike. When present, the branches define the equation and `rhs` may be omitted.
Primary engine (must appear in environment.requirements; migration target replacing deprecated 'software').
Observed improvement relative to baseline based on a defined score.
Add the location of the data file containing the parcellation terminology.

Path of a file that lists the members, read each time the cohort is used, so a list its producer keeps (the subjects a pipeline has finished) is never copied into the recipe. A ``.yaml`` or ``.json`` file holds what ``members`` would hold; a ``.tsv`` or ``.csv`` file is a participants table (the BIDS ``participants.tsv`` layout, tab- or comma-separated), read by its ``participant_id`` column, and a row with a value but no participant is an error; any other file holds one identifier per line, blank lines and lines starting with ``#`` skipped. Members come in the file's order and a ``sub-`` prefix is dropped. A relative path is read from the directory of the experiment or network file the dataset is part of, also when the dataset comes into that file by ``!include`` from another directory, and, when the file is not there, from the root of the study that file belongs to; a missing file is an error naming the places tried. Messages about a list read from a file give counts and positions, never an identifier.

A rule on a phenotype measure that admits the members (``CohortRule``): one group of a split of the subjects by a score. The members are computed from the phenotype table each time the cohort is used, so no list is typed or stored.
Globally unique identifier for the entity.
Add the location of the data file containing the parcellation terminology.

The subject identifiers this cohort holds, without the ``sub-`` prefix, in the order a stacked read returns them. When the enclosing dataset lists its ``subjects``, every member must be one of them. A cohort states its members in exactly one way: typed here, read from ``members_file``, or admitted by ``rule``.
Identifier of a cohort, unique within the study: the name a reference addresses it by (``used: {cohort: <id>}``). Corresponds to the BIDS ``cohort-`` entity.
Human-readable session label.
Human-readable label for the subject.
Human-readable dataset name.
Human-readable cohort name.
What admits a subject to this cohort, in words: the selection rule, the site, the diagnostic group.
Ordered magnitudes with no meaningful zero. The scale an undeclared continuous mark takes, and what `image.cmap` is set to.
Spatial coordinates (x, y, z) of the node

comment.en: Anatomical region(s) the Dynamics model is intended to represent. Range: UBERON terms.

definition.value: Number of identical cells this node represents as a population. The default (1) is a single unit; size>1 makes the node a population of N cells sharing this node's dynamics, addressed by index 0..N-1 when a connectivity rule on an incident Edge is expanded. Maps to a NeuroML <population size="N">. Backend-independent: it states the population's cardinality, not a storage layout.
bsplot mosaic string; letters = panel keys, slash (or newline) = new row, repeated letters span cells, dot = empty. e.g. aab/ccb.
List of directed edges with coupling references (optional, for explicit edge definition)

The published figure this one reproduces, as a path relative to the study root (e.g. original_study/img/fig_04.png). Names the A/B target for `tvbo figure compare`, which measures panel geometry against it; it is never a data source, and never rendered into a panel.
A `dseg` segmentation file, for a parcellation nobody has curated.
How voxels collapse along the view axis (`absmax` by default).
BEP017 measure names for observational targets (e.g., BoldCorrelation)

Representation used to evaluate coupling over this network's connectivity (``auto`` | ``dense`` | ``sparse``). ``auto`` lets the backend choose by connection density. This names whether to exploit edge sparsity, not a concrete data structure, so it is backend-independent; the delayed-vs-instantaneous graph kind is decided separately from the couplings' conduction delays.

Makes this network a subset by node of what it declares (``NodeSelection``): the nodes to keep or to drop, named by label. Everything else is as declared, so a network that includes another and adds a selection is that network without some of its nodes.
Dynamics model governing this node's behavior. Can be a reference (by name) or inline definition. If not provided, uses experiment's dynamics.

Number of nodes in the network, derived from `nodes` when it lists them. Beside a source (an `iri`, a `data_file`, a `bids_dir` or the curated network of a `parcellation`) it is the number of the source's nodes the network keeps: all of them at the source's own count, and below it a random subset drawn once at build from `execution.random_seed`, which `node_selection` then names. A count above the source's is refused.
Reference to tractography data

Ordered list of transforms applied to edge property matrices. Each entry rewrites the edge property its `output:` names, else the one its `name:` is (e.g. 'weight', 'length'), and that property is also the value under transform inside the entry's own equation, which is written over the network's edge attributes. Supports equation-based (symbolic) or callable-based (software) transforms. Multiple transforms on the same target are applied sequentially, each seeing the previous one's output; since `name:` identifies an entry, each after the first states the target as its `output:`.
W3C PROV-O aligned provenance for this entity — what it was derived from, which agent produced it, and when.

comment.en: The task is only well-posed on a backend that provides the named capability.

definition.value: Panel-letter size in points. Unset scales it above the body font_size by the theme's `panel_number_scale`, the convention most journals follow — a letter set at the body size reads as a tick label rather than as the panel's name.

Importable module names whose import registers this figure's custom panels / transforms (via bsplot.register_panel / register_transform). The emitted plot.py imports them, so a study ships its bespoke figure code in its code_source instead of in core tvbo. The modules must be importable when the figure renders (loading the study puts its code/ dir on the path).
Globally unique identifier for the entity.

Name of the edge whose matrix is the network's weights: ``matrix("weight")`` reads it, and a save writes the weights under it. Lets a single Network sidecar bundle several connectivity variants (e.g. band-specific NMF reweightings, distance-modulated SC, shuffled controls) under different edge names while presenting one of them as the weights to consumers (simulators, observation pipelines). Without it the weights are the ``weight`` edge; a network that holds its weights under another name (``sc``, ``weights``) declares that name here, and is refused naming the edge until it does.
W3C PROV-O aligned provenance for this entity — what it was derived from, which agent produced it, and when.
BIDS filename entities for this dataset
Short alphanumeric identifier for the BIDS desc- filename entity (e.g., SC, FC, EC, SCFC). Classifies the connectivity modality of the network's edge measures.
Unit for distances/lengths in the network
Panel groups that share one y scale, each entry a comma-separated list of mosaic keys ('c,g,h'). Same rule as share_x.
Relative heights of the mosaic rows, e.g. [1.15, 1, 1, 1] to make the top panel taller. Length = number of rows.
Panels keyed by their mosaic label.

Which part of a generated report this belongs in — the main Methods or the supplementary material. Placement only: every experiment runs and every figure renders regardless, so demoting one never changes what is computed. It answers a different question from a replication's target tier (how central a claim is) and from the source paper's own Fig/EDF numbering (where *they* printed it), because our document may carry a headline result's parameter dump in the SI, or relegate a figure the paper printed up front. Defaults to ``main``, so a recipe that says nothing keeps everything in the Methods.

Whether this figure's axes follow a theme's axis rule. `false` leaves every axis exactly as its panels drew it, whatever the study's theme says: no tick re-placed, no limit moved, no spine detached or trimmed, no labels aligned. `true` draws it by the curated `tvbo:themes/bsplot` rule wherever neither its own theme nor its study's states one. Unset follows the theme.
Author display strings (full detail in references.bib).
BibTeX citation key; the join key into references.bib for full bibliographic detail. A study is identified by its key/citekey and described by its title — no ``name`` needed.
Ordered list of subject IDs (e.g. HCP-YA 6-digit IDs). Each ``measures/<name>`` array in the h5 companion is indexed by this order.
Reference to empirical data observation for matching objectives
Metric equation for matching (e.g., correlation, rmse)

Turns the figure into a movie over one dimension of its data instead of a still. Every other field keeps its meaning — the mosaic, the panels, the sizing and the styling are the frame; the animation only says which dimension advances and how fast. Declaring it is what makes a figure whose subject is a *process* show the process rather than a snapshot of it, without a second, hand-written plotting path.
Relative widths of the mosaic columns.
Git branch, tag, or commit to check out (``git`` sources only). Defaults to the repository's default branch.
Target value for activity objectives
Subdirectory within the source to place on the import path (defaults to the source root).
HDF5 dataset path for node-to-parent mapping. Int32 array of shape (N,) where entry i is the parent node ID. Required when parent_network is set.
Git repository URL to fetch the code from (shallow-cloned and cached under ``~/.cache/tvbo/code_sources``). Mutually exclusive with ``path``.
The ``tvbo study init --template`` name this seed belongs to.

The datasets this study reads per-subject files from, each with the cohorts defined over it (``Dataset.cohorts``). Declared here, at the study, a dataset is visible to every analysis and experiment, so a reference names a cohort by identifier alone (``used: {cohort: <id>}``).

Other studies this one aggregates, each a ``SimulationStudy`` in its own right — so a study-of-studies is the same class as the studies it holds, and nesting recurses to any depth without a wrapper class standing between a study and the studies it holds. A whole manuscript is then one runnable specification whose sub-studies are runnable specifications. Written as ``!include <path>`` so each sub-study keeps its own recipe file and therefore its own directory: its ``code_source``, its results root and its relative references all resolve against where it lives, not against whoever included it. ``tvbo run`` walks the nested studies depth first, then runs the owning study's own experiments, analyses and figures — the paper-native content belonging to no sub-study. Legitimized by COMBINE/OMEX, SED-ML and the ISA ``Investigation`` top-level container it parallels.

Optional stable IRI (or compact URI) for this entity in an external ontology or knowledge base. Used to load metadata from an external source; not required when the entity is fully self-contained (equations, parameters, etc. defined in the file itself).

Analyses of this study's results, each persisted as its own container and so bindable by a figure or a later analysis exactly like a run. These take the ``Analysis`` form that invokes a ``callable`` over ``arguments`` (the ``type``/``target``/``wrt`` form analyses a solve and belongs on an ``Observation`` instead), and each needs a unique ``name`` — it keys the container. An argument's ``used:`` DataRef both records what was consumed and orders the run: ``tvbo run`` executes the analyses around the experiments — one an experiment consumes first, one consuming an experiment after — and then renders the figures.

WHERE + WHICH + SLICE in one edge — this parameter's array sourced from another experiment's result (an operating point, a tuned ``estimate__<name>`` a fit persisted), a dataset, or a curated entity, PROV ``prov:used``. The full cross-container form of which `source:`+`measure:` is the no-``sel``/no-``experiment`` shorthand; adds label ``reconcile`` and a swept-point ``sel``. Like `source:` the array is resolved lazily and never inlined. An in-study ``experiment`` reference also registers the workflow dependency. Mutually exclusive with `value:`/`source:`/`producer:`.
Bind the key to a computed scalar in a result container (same reference form a figure Layer uses, and the same PROV edge). Mutually exclusive with ``value`` and ``count``.

A labelled array sourced from another experiment's result, a dataset, or a curated entity — the cross-container form of a value (WHERE + WHICH + SLICE, PROV ``prov:used``). Mutually exclusive with ``value``; an in-study ``experiment`` reference also registers the workflow dependency so the source runs first. Resolved lazily, never inlined into generated code.

WHERE + WHICH + SLICE for a template edge whose whole matrix is read rather than stored or computed: another network's layer, an analysis result, or a cohort member's own connectome (``used: {cohort: <id>, query: {...}, output: weight, reconcile: by_label}``). Inside a per-subject run a cohort reference resolves to that run's subject, which is what binds a model network to each subject's own connectivity. ``reconcile: by_label`` aligns the read matrix to this network's node order through its atlas aliases. Resolved lazily and never inlined, and it wins over a same-named layer in the companion file. Mutually exclusive with ``producer:``.
The p-value, a scalar in a result container (same reference form a Layer uses, and the same PROV edge).
IRIs of the inputs, outputs and environment the activity consumed (BEP028 ``Used``).

Bind the annotation to a scalar in a result container (same reference form a Layer uses, and the same PROV edge). The referenced value is formatted through `text` at render time, so a statistic printed on a panel is computed, never transcribed.

Covariance of the unit-intensity noise increment across the axis named by `correlated_over` — the second-order structure of the driving process, stated as mathematics rather than as a factorisation. Must be square in that axis, symmetric and positive semi-definite; its diagonal carries per-element variances and need NOT be unity, so unequal variances and cross-element correlation are expressed together. The realised increment is the declared sigma times a draw from this covariance, so `parameters: {sigma: ...}` continues to mean what it means for uncorrelated noise. Absent (the default) means the increment is independent across that axis. Being a `Parameter`, it carries the full provenance triple: a literal `value:`, existing bytes via `source:`+`measure:`, or — the usual case for a derived operator — `producer:`, whose FunctionCall records how the structure was obtained (projecting a spatially white field into a modal basis, spreading independent per-region drives through a connectome). The generative account therefore lives in the provenance, and the matrix itself stays a statement about the process. How a backend samples it (Cholesky, eigendecomposition, whitening) is a backend concern and is never stated here.

Where this study's callable code lives — the builders and transform/observation callables it references by bare ``module:`` name. Decouples the specification from its code: a local directory (relative to the recipe YAML or absolute) or a git repository fetched and cached at load time. When absent, the conventional ``<recipe-dir>/code/`` is used.
Indicates whether the noise is Gaussian
Indicates whether the noise is additive
Cartesian mark; omitted for heatmap panels (implied by the panel kind).
Deprecated. Whether the noise is correlated, without saying across which axis or by how much. Use `covariance` + `correlated_over`.
Fill only this triangle of a square matrix, masking the other half so a sibling layer fills it. Two layers then compose one matrix image whose halves are the quantities being compared.
Distance from a panel title to the axes, in points.

Seed for the noise the settle integrates, when the settle runs as its own scan. Absent -- the default -- leaves the settle on whatever stream its solver hands it, which is what an unmodified upstream warm start does; the backend is not silently given a different draw than the reference implementation it is checked against. Present means the settle uses exactly this seed. Both interesting cases are then sayable: equal to `seed` puts the two scans on one stream, and different from it decorrelates them. Equal is not neutral -- where the two scans take the same number of steps a shorter draw is a prefix of a longer one, so the measured noise repeats the settle's sample for sample, and corr(settle, measured) on demeaned fluctuations is +0.49 against -0.01 decorrelated. Its effect on the reported statistics was null everywhere it was measured (FC bias below 0.03 sigma, no trend), so this slot exists to make the choice visible and reproducible rather than because either answer is known to be wrong.
Length of the caps on an error bar, in points. 0 draws none.
Keep text as text in vector output (embedded TrueType in PDF and PostScript, live text in SVG), so a typesetter can edit a label instead of receiving outlines.

Which axis `covariance` indexes — `node` (equivalently `region`) for spatially correlated drive, or `state` for correlation between the noise on different state variables. Required whenever `covariance` is set: a covariance without a named axis does not identify a process. A multi-mode model carries its modes inside the state axis, so a modal covariance is declared over `state`.

Temporal character of the process: `gaussian`/`white` (delta-correlated in time) or `ou`/`ornstein-uhlenbeck` (exponentially correlated in time). Governs the TIME axis only, and composes freely with `covariance`, which governs a spatial axis.
State variables this noise applies to; if omitted, applies globally.
Line weight of the axes grid, in points. Ignored unless `grid_lines` is set.
Length of a minor tick mark, in points. Ignored unless `minor_ticks` is set.
The most ticks a `round` axis carries. Unset is 4. A panel that states its own `nbins` keeps the backend's locator on that budget instead.
BIDS-compatible subject identifier (without 'sub-' prefix). Examples: '01', 'ctrl03', 'patient17'.
Age at time of study (years).
Depth channel for a line3d panel (the third phase-space axis); ignored by 2-D kinds.
How far an axis extends past its data where its end is not on a tick, as a fraction of the data's span. Unset keeps the backend's own margin.
Line weight of the outline of a bar or any other filled patch, in points.
Dash pattern of the axes grid. Ignored unless `grid_lines` is set.
Human-readable session label.
Human-readable label for the subject.
Human-readable dataset name.
Human-readable cohort name.
Biological sex.
Data collection sessions for this subject. Each session can have its own network, empirical data, and conditions.
Additional subject metadata as key-value pairs or path to a sidecar JSON file.
Size of legend text as a multiple of the body size. Unset draws it at the body size.
Declarative Figure specs rendered from this study's experiment results — closes the replication loop (a study is its experiments plus the figures that read them).
How to package the run into a COMBINE/OMEX archive — the single supplementary artifact from which every figure, number and caption regenerates. Unset means no archive is emitted.

The named numbers the prose cites, each keyed by the manuscript token that stands in for it (``key``) and bound either to a computed value (``used:`` a DataRef into this study's or a nested study's analysis) or to an authored constant quoted from prior work (``value`` + ``source``). ``tvbo run`` collects these into a results manifest the document reads, so no reported figure is transcribed by hand and a stale or missing key fails the build rather than printing a wrong number.
Non-visual grouping dim (e.g. the hue/iterate dim).
Distance from an axis label to its axis, in points. The default for a panel's own `xlabel_pad`/`ylabel_pad`.
Distance from a tick mark to its label, in points.
BIDS ``DatasetType`` this layout realises, written into the dataset's ``dataset_description.json``.

Panel groups that share one x scale, each entry a comma-separated list of mosaic keys ('c,g,h'). Every panel in a group ends on the union of the group's limits. Declare it whenever a panel's tick labels are hidden as another panel's: hiding them alone asserts a shared scale the axes do not actually have, and a reader then compares two panels drawn at different ranges.

Per-figure HPC/workflow resource refinement (reuses WorkflowConfig, same pattern as SimulationExperiment.workflow_overrides); lets a heavy render request its own resources when figures are emitted as workflow jobs. The figure's Layer.used edges become the render rule's input dependencies.
Reference to raw or thresholded volume
Native library/module providing the callable.
Globally unique identifier for the entity.
Ordered parameter names passed to the callable.
BIDS version the layout was written against.

The kinds of study this record covers, keyed by the name ``tvbo study init --template`` takes. An entry's ``in_templates`` names one of these, so a template that nothing declares is a typo rather than a silently empty variant.
Globally unique identifier for the entity.
One dash pattern per entry of a standalone legend.

comment.en: Range is a reified BifurcationEvent that records the bifurcation type, the locus parameter, and (optionally) the critical value.

Hardware accelerator the run targets. 'auto' (default) lets JAX detect the machine — GPU/TPU when present, else CPU; 'cpu', 'gpu', or 'tpu' pin the JAX platform explicitly. tvbo maps this to JAX_PLATFORMS before JAX initialises (an existing JAX_PLATFORMS in the environment still wins); tvboptim then spreads work across that platform's devices via n_pmap/n_vmap. In a workflow kit, 'gpu' also makes the experiment's rule request a SLURM gres unless one is set.

System size (van Kampen Ω) for the stochastic 'gillespie' backend: the number of discrete units per unit of the activity variable, and the sole source of noise. Runs a mean-field rate model as a finite birth-death process (Gillespie SSA): the activity state variable X becomes a discrete count n ≈ Ω·X, its relaxation equation tau*X' = -X + F(...) is read as birth propensity Ω·F/tau (the gain) and death propensity n/tau (the leak), while the remaining state variables integrate deterministically between events. Larger Ω means finer discreteness and weaker fluctuations, recovering the deterministic mean field as Ω→∞. For an activity already expressed as a fraction in [0,1], Ω is the population size N; for a firing rate it is N divided by the rate at full activation. Required by the 'gillespie' backend; ignored by every other backend.

Backend-neutral numerical treatment of the network coupling term across the stages of a multi-stage integrator (Heun, RK4, ...): re-evaluated at every stage (per_stage, standard ODE accuracy) or computed once per step and held across the stages (per_step, the TVB scheme). A single-stage method (Euler) and a single node integrate the same system under both. tvboptim's native solvers, NetworkDynamics.jl and the jax backend honour both values, the jax backend per_stage over an undelayed coupling only; TVB and the Python graph runner integrate per_step and refuse per_stage, and tvboptim's diffrax solvers and PyRates always integrate per_stage, whatever is declared (CouplingStageEvaluation states each value's behaviour). per_stage is required to match reference integrators for stiff, chaotic or multistable systems, where the frozen-coupling error can select a different trajectory or attractor.

Absent (``null``) means require full coverage (``1.0``) for a dataset-sourced target — silently fitting on a partial node subset must be an explicit opt-in (e.g. ``0.95`` to tolerate a few genuinely-missing empirical parcels), never the default.

A name no network parameter carries, one without ``levels``, a count of codes other than this vocabulary's entry count, and a code outside the parent vocabulary are refused when the network is resolved.

The ontology classes this record is an instance of (`tvbo:GlobalCouplingScaling`). A class membership, where `iri` is the record's own address and `grounding` names what it stands in for.

Length of the leading settling window, prepended to `duration`. It marks part of ONE integration — never a separate simulation: the backend integrates `transient_time + duration` in a single scan and the marked head is cut where the run is consumed (observations, analyses, plots, saved data), so the settle is in-band for any observation kernel that needs warm-up. Time is measured from the START of the measured window: the settle carries non-positive timestamps and ends at 0, the measured window opens one step later, and a declared event `t0` is relative to measurement, never to the scan. A settle that a fit reuses across many candidate evaluations is NOT this slot — that is a seed, declared as `initial_state.method: time_integration` with its own `duration`.

Unit of every time-valued number in this scope — the step size, any period, and the physical meaning of one model time-step. Declared at whichever scope owns the clock (network, integrator, observation); `tvbo.utils.units.time_unit_of` resolves a scope to its effective unit by walking outwards, and states the `ms` fallback once, at the end of that walk. Deliberately carries no default: a defaulted slot cannot be inherited through, so `ifabsent: ms` made an unset unit indistinguishable from one someone wrote, and masked an explicitly declared `s` one scope out. `time_scale` is accepted as a synonym.

Optional stable IRI (or compact URI) for this entity in an external ontology or knowledge base. Used to load metadata from an external source; not required when the entity is fully self-contained (equations, parameters, etc. defined in the file itself).
Dynamics model governing this node's behavior. Can be a reference (by name) or inline definition. If not provided, uses experiment's dynamics.

Arguments handed to whatever resolves `source`, such as the normalisation or the conduction velocity a per-node measure is computed with. They travel with the parameter so a spec states not only where a value comes from but how it is derived, and a resolver refuses an argument it does not know.

HOW to compute this value, when it is derived rather than obtained — the callable that produces it, its arguments, and (via `output:`) which entry to take from a callable returning several named arrays. The callable resolves against the recipe's `code_source`. Use instead of `source:` for a value that is a deterministic function of the spec's own inputs (a mesh operator, a template matrix): declaring the producer keeps the spec the single source of truth, where pointing at a pre-built file would let the two drift apart silently — and would need a prep step run by hand before the spec could execute. The result is cached and invalidated by the artifact fingerprint, so it is computed once rather than per run. On a `Parameter` it produces the value; on an `Edge` it produces the whole template matrix, which is what lets a connectome or a discrete differential operator be declared rather than pre-built. Mutually exclusive with `value:`/`source:`.
Whether a value for this parameter must be supplied. Optional parameters (e.g. a generator's ``seed``) set this to false. Declaration metadata; unset means unconstrained.

WHICH array to select out of `source`. The address space is the source's own: a per-node measure name for a Network (aligning with Network.structural_measures / observational_measures), a dataset key for an HDF5/Zarr store, a recorded measure for an experiment result. Omit when the source resolves to a single array. Without a `source`, or beside the CSV a CSV save writes for it, it is the array's path in the network's own companion (``nodes/parent_index``), and on a ``node_template`` parameter that array runs over the nodes: node ``i`` takes its entry ``i``, so it has one entry per node, and one of another length is refused when the network is read or saved.

Declared value type of this parameter, given as a schema range name — a primitive (``integer``, ``float``, ``string``, ``uriorcurie``) or a class (e.g. ``Distribution``). Documents the expected type when the parameter is a *declaration* carrying no concrete ``value`` (e.g. a GraphGenerator's typed argument interface). Distinct from ``domain`` (numeric bounds) and ``unit``.

Free-text provenance tag on each submitted job (Slurm ``--comment``), visible in ``squeue -o %k``. Unset means an auto-generated ``tvbo:<study>/exp_<experiment>`` tag so a queued job maps back to its experiment; set it to override with a custom string.

Numeric, string, or boolean value, OR an array (nested list) for array-valued constants such as mode-coupling coefficient matrices. ScalarValue accepts any literal primitive type, allowing parameters to carry control flags (e.g., booleans) or symbolic placeholders alongside numeric defaults.

External ontology IRIs (typically GO, ChEBI, UBERON, CL, MeSH) that this entity is a surrogate / abstraction / model of. Realized as the `tvbo:surrogate_of` object property, carried inline with the YAML data instance. Multiple IRIs allowed: a single parameter may abstract several biological processes (e.g. a synaptic conductance grounding both GO:0060079 (excitatory PSP) and GO:0007268 (chemical synaptic transmission)).
